Technical concept diagram, captioned "Figure 2. Quasi Earth Fixed NTN Cell". Appears directly after the Same-PLMN/Roaming/RAN-Sharing integration-models figure, illustrating how a non-geostationary satellite constellation maintains a fixed-position cell on the Earth's surface across a satellite handover.

Two satellite boxes at the top, "Incoming satellite — Non-Geostationary Satellite B" (left) and "Outgoing satellite — Non-Geostationary Satellite A" (right), with an arrow labelled "Direction of motion of the satellites" pointing from B's position toward A's, showing the constellation moving left to right.

Below, an ellipse labelled "Cell (quasi-earth-fixed)" contains two clusters of small circles/beams:
- A cluster of plain white/grey circles, annotated "Non-Geostationary-satellite beam after hand over to satellite B" (arrow from the left, from Satellite B).
- A cluster of hatched/shaded circles labelled "TA" (Tracking Area), annotated "Non-Geostationary-satellite beam before satellite A hand over" (arrow from the right, from Satellite A).

The diagram illustrates that as the satellite constellation moves, the serving satellite for a given ground-fixed cell changes (handover from outgoing Satellite A to incoming Satellite B), while the cell itself — and its Tracking Area — remains fixed relative to the Earth's surface, which is the "quasi-earth-fixed" cell behavior referenced in 3GPP NTN.
